title: Feeling bad about being left behind, and why managers refuse unsolicited tunes
summary: Fats told the band he left it to Kirkeby; Autrey explains how hearing thousands of submitted tunes leads to unconscious copying and suits.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x:
Well then how -- in view of that,
when, for example, Fats went off to Europe and left the band
behind, goes off to California and leaves the band behind,
how did this affect your relationship with Fats? Did you feel
bad about it? Or say anything? (inaudible)?
Well I felt bad about it, but I didn't -- still didn't blame Fats, because I knew why, and Fats didn't do it. And Kirkoby did it. That's what I mean.
Did FATS ever say anything to you about it? About --

Afterwards, no, he said fellows, I'm sorry, but -- I left it up to Ed. He said, I don't know. I, you know, what Ed -- he used to sell this, don't you worry about the business, you worry about your music. Leave the business to us, to the office. You know, because we don't want to have you concerned about this, or worrying about that. It's like so many people walk up to you in the theater, or here or there, oh, Mr. Autrey, Mr. Waller, Mr. so and so, I wrote some tunes. I wrote a tune. I know it's going to be a hit. Will you please listen to -- you know, everything. You hear that every day. Thousands of times a day, if you let yourself, you know. And after you hear so doggone many tunes, you will hear it, and you will rewrite that damn tune. You're not -- you're not aware of it. I mean it's embedded into your brain, your subconscious, or whatever you want to call it. I mean the guy -- if there was somebody that was more intelligent he could say -- he'd know exactly where it comes from. So when you put it on paper, then they call you a thief. The man stole my tune.
There have been loads of suits based on that. Kind of hard to prove, though, sometimes.

Yes, it's so. What happens, a good smart manager tell his client, tell his agent, don't listen to nobody's tune. Don't do it. Write your own, and let them have theirs, and keep it -- one of those things. See.
